title: Can anyone see the report?
hook: Would a visible false report feel the same as a private one?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish observability of dishonesty from the material payoff to lying.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish observability of dishonesty from the material payoff to lying.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy lie gains €5 and has an 80% chance of a €10 penalty. What is its expected net payoff? Toy inputs A=[5, 0.8, 10]; B=[5, 0, 10].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[-3, 8, 5], [5, 0, 5]]. Labels: Expected net €, Expected penalty €, Gain €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Observability can change a detection probability while leaving the gain from lying fixed. The comparison separates that risk from the material reward. These are explicit toy probabilities rather than measured deterrence or honesty rates.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Gain €=5, Detection P=0, Penalty €=10. What is Expected net €? Answer: 5.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Gain €=5, Detection P=0, Penalty €=10. What is Expected net €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 5. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: People lie less when others can see the lie (Gneezy, Kajackaite & Sobel, 2018).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish observability of dishonesty from the material payoff to lying.
